ios.desc:
Timber turns readers into listeners. Anything you want to read, you can listen to instead.

Paste a link, drop in a PDF, open a book, or snap a photo of a printed page. Timber pulls out the real text, cleanly, and reads it aloud in a voice you pick. There is a companion desktop app that moves your open browser tabs into your ears.

Ever asked your phone to read a page aloud and had it stop halfway, or skip the part that mattered? That is not you missing a setting. Most reader tools are not built to get the whole article. Timber pulls the full text out first, before it ever starts speaking. What you paste is what you hear, start to finish.

It was built by a teacher, after watching students struggle to read, who could not find one app that read well, respected privacy, and did not hold the basics hostage.

WHAT TIMBER PROMISES
• No account. No sign-up. Open it and read.
• The core reader is free, and stays free.
• What you read is nobody's business. Articles, books and clipboard text are processed on your device. What you read is never shared, sold, or used for ads.

VOICES, PROPERLY
• 300+ voices across 71 languages, free, spoken entirely on your device.
• Every Apple voice on your device works, free, including Enhanced and Premium.
• Every voice library includes a free male and female voice in your language. No teaser locked behind a trial.
• Record a reference of your own voice and Timber can read in it. Created on device, never uploaded.

A READER THAT FEELS LIKE PAPER
• Warm parchment design. An open book under a reading lamp, not a tech product.
• Every word lights up as it is spoken, and keeps pace whether you slow it right down or push it fast.
• Tune the size, the face and the line spacing until it is comfortable. 30 palettes built in, plus a full dyslexia mode.

BRING ANYTHING
• Paste a link and Timber extracts the article. No ads, no popups, just the text.
• Share from Safari or any browser. Import PDFs, EPUB, Word and PowerPoint. Follow RSS feeds.
• Point your camera at a printed page and Timber reads it back to you.
• Scanned chapters carry junk on every page. Timber spots a line that repeats and silences it across the whole document in one tap.
• Browse 70,000+ free public-domain books from Project Gutenberg.
• Translate an article on device, or get a quick summary on device. No cloud, no AI account.
• Export any article as spoken audio to take with you.
• Optional iCloud sync keeps your library on all your devices.

FOR CLASSROOMS AND STUDY
•

quotes.text:
If you use Safari Reader, you already know it sometimes gets half of an article, or nothing at all. The  read-aloud stops early, and you’re back to scrolling.
Timber on iPhone/iPad/Mac, is my answer to that problem. Anything you can read can be read to you in hundreds of free voices among thousands of available ones, even cloning your own in seconds.

Timber Tabs, on the Mac, takes the pile of browser tabs you have been meaning to read (Safari/Chrome/Firefox/Edge/etc) and sends them to your phone. Both are free, both are on the App Store, and neither one spams you or asks you for a special account.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/timber-text-to-speech-voice/id6779086700

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/timber-tabs-talking-websites/id6786080053

So much more than just Ollama for Text to Speech Audio – 6 different of the latest LLM models that run offline: Piper, Kokoro, Kitten, Supertonic, and two personal-voice engines Pocket and MOSS, plus Apple's own. 3,801 voices you can pick, 324 of them free, across 71 languages and dialects. Words light up as they are spoken, and the highlighting was just as difficult as the text extraction. That last sentence is most of why this took as long as it did.
Timber Tabs reads your open Safari and Chrome tabs, filters out the video and the web apps, lets you pick, and sends a list of articles to your phone through your own iCloud. Titles and links only.

Timber only talks to the network when you ask it to. A link you paste. A free book. A feed …
quotes.story_title: Show HN: Timber (iOS) and Timber Tabs (Mac) – best offline read-aloud LLMs
